doors.label: I'm about to invest or acquire in a company
proposals: Could they survive a ransomware week?
What is fixable, what's a deal-breaker
doors.note: Technical opinion, not financial advice. We do not assess a deal and then sell fixes to the same target.

slides.heading: Identify risks and prevent cybersecurity-related losses before they happen.
slides.body: A data leak, a critical vulnerability not fixed: each one lands on the buyer after closing.

slides.heading: An independent read, before you sign.
slides.example: We test how the company responds to an incident, not just which policies exist.

slides.heading: A lower bill, or a different price.
slides.body: You get red flags ranked by what they could cost, and which ones are fixable and which are deal-breakers.

doors.label: I run a company
proposals: To prove our security to a customer or an insurer
Be ready before a raise or an exit

slides.heading: Prove your cybersecurity level to customers, insurers and investors.
slides.body: Most small companies can't explain what is in place to protect their data and their customers' data.

slides.heading: We find it before they do.
slides.example: We perform a practical review of what attackers and due-diligence teams would find, then we provide a short fix list in priority order.

slides.heading: Raise the value, not just the defences.
slides.body: Clean answers in the data room, better insurance terms, bigger customers.

doors.label: I lead an IT or Cybersecurity team
proposals: A second pair of experienced eyes

slides.heading: Cut the noise and focus on the risks that matter.
slides.body: Good teams still lose time to noise and to the gaps between tools.

slides.heading: Operational help, alongside your team.
slides.example: We improve detection and response playbooks, based on real incident work.

slides.heading: Calmer nights.
slides.body: Clear owners, tested runbooks and fewer surprises.

doors.label: I build with AI or agents
proposals: Where can our agents be hijacked?
Limit what it can do when fooled

slides.heading: Stop your AI agents from being manipulated into harmful actions.
slides.body: Any page, document or tool output it reads is a place for someone else's instructions.

slides.heading: Map where it can be hijacked.
slides.example: Test input path, permissions to understand what an attacker can gain.

slides.heading: Recovery, not just alerts.
slides.body: A defined pause and reset path before the bad day.

doors.label: I've just been compromised
proposals: A plan for the next hours
Help on who to notify, and when

slides.heading: Contain the incident and keep the evidence.
We've done this many times.
slides.example: Isolate the affected machines from the network, keep them powered and write down what you saw and when.

slides.heading: A plan for the next hour.
slides.body: Book a call now and we'll triage together.

doors.label: I need to know where I stand on SOC2, CRA, NIS2
proposals: Does it apply to my company?
What is already ok, what's missing

slides.heading: Know which cybersecurity regulations apply and where you stand.
slides.body: NIS2, DORA and the Cyber Resilience Act add duties, deadlines and penalties.

slides.heading: A plain-language gap check.
slides.example: We identify what applies to your business, what is already done and what to do first.

slides.heading: No surprise audits.
slides.body: A short, ordered plan you can act on.
